# Galaxy Watch7 vs Galaxy Watch Ultra: Samsung Smartwatches 2024

![]()
![]()

## Galaxy Watch7 vs Galaxy Watch Ultra: Latest Samsung Smartwatches 2024

With an impressive array of health and fitness tracking capabilities, the [Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra](https://www.samsung.com/uk/watches/galaxy-watch-ultra/buy/) and [Watch7](https://www.samsung.com/uk/watches/galaxy-watch7/buy/) are the latest smartwatches to join the [Samsung wearables family](https://www.samsung.com/uk/watches/galaxy-watch/). In this guide, we explore their new and upgraded features, including how Galaxy AI is set to maximise your health and wellbeing like never before.

## What's the Galaxy Watch7 and Galaxy Watch Ultra release date?

The next generation of Galaxy watches were launched at Samsung’s Unpacked Event on the 10th July 2024, with sales starting on the 24th July 2024. They build on the success of the [Galaxy Watch6 Classic](https://www.samsung.com/uk/watches/all-watches/?galaxy-watch-classic) and [Galaxy Watch6](https://www.samsung.com/uk/watches/galaxy-watch/galaxy-watch6-44mm-silver-lte-sm-r945fzsaeua/) Galaxy Watch6 which were released the previous year in July 2023.  
  
The latest Samsung smartwatches bring with them a more powerful processor, high-precision GPS, and next-gen BioActiveSensors. What’s more, they now have [Galaxy AI](https://www.samsung.com/uk/galaxy-ai/)  pumping through their circuits, so it’s like having your own private coach that never clocks off, constantly analysing data from the day to best prepare you for the next.

## Galaxy Watch7 price & features

Everyday wellness starts with Samsung Galaxy Watch7 and the latest generation of Galaxy AI. Available in two different sizes (40mm and 44mm), the Galaxy Watch7 features a one-click rubber strap and scratch resistant Sapphire Crystal Glass display offering a premium look and feel.  
  
An all-new Exynos processor enables Galaxy AI to work at full capacity to guide you on your health and wellness journey. You can lift the lid on the different stages of every evening’s sleep, getting to know what makes you tick and learn about how you can improve your overall wellbeing. The Energy Score compiles your key health data into one, easy to understand number, then offers tailored, habit-changing suggestions in the form of Wellness Tips1 to help drive you towards your wellness goals. All of your favourites are onboard too, including Body Composition2, ECG, Blood Pressure3 and women’s health tracking4. Plus, you can now stay focused on the task at hand with Smart Replies5 – the Galaxy AI feature that writes replies in your style and voice by analysing previous conversations.

![]()
![]()

It pairs effortlessly with the [Samsung ecosystem](https://www.samsung.com/uk/mobile-phone-buying-guide/supporting-products/), bringing messages, calls and notifications to the wrist. And when you need to travel light, just leave your phone at home because the Galaxy Watch7 has its own LTE connectivity6. Skip songs playing through your new Galaxy Buds3 Pro, pay in just a tap with [Samsung Wallet](https://www.samsung.com/uk/apps/samsung-wallet/)7 and track down other devices using [Samsung Find](https://www.samsung.com/uk/apps/smartthings-find/)8. Whether you’re counting daily steps or smashing weeknight workouts, the Galaxy Watch7 unlocks your health goals, so you can exercise better and live healthier.  
  
The Galaxy Watch7 is £289.00 when retailing at full price.

![]()
![]()

## Galaxy Watch Ultra price & features

The Galaxy Watch Ultra is the smartwatch that knows no bounds. With a timeless design built to withstand the harshest environments; it’s an endurance athlete’s dream. With a 47mm watch face, distinctive titanium casing, and a tactile strap, it’s as tough as it is rugged. In fact, it’s been tested to military standards and can withstand altitudes between -500m and 9,000m. It is also resistant to temperatures between -20°C and 55°C, and has 10ATM pressure-resistance up to 100m in water1. Whether the latest epic challenge sees you up a mountain, in the shallows1 or somewhere in between the Galaxy Watch Ultra is built to go above and beyond.  
  
It’s also home to a raft of finely tuned tech optimised to meet the most demanding challenges. The customisable Quick Button provides a quick and precise way of logging lap times, ending workouts or pausing timers. Should the worst happen, an emergency siren up to 86dB can be sounded and is audible up to 180m away2. It even features a time-sensitive night vision face which automatically kicks in when the sun goes down.

![]()
![]()

And that’s not all. The Galaxy Watch Ultra is Samsung’s most AI-enhanced smartwatch to date. After setting your goals in Samsung Health, Galaxy AI will offer a daily Energy Score, backed up by Wellness Tips3 to help motivate you towards your targets. The score takes into account how well you slept and how much you exercised the day before, to guide you on how to get the most out of your day. When it’s time to lace up your trainers, you can activate Race4 to challenge your previous times and set new PBs. And to make sure you don’t lose focus in the middle of a workout session or meditation hour, Smart Replies5 can now mimic your writing style by analysing previous conversations, so you can stay focused on what matters.  
  
The all-new Exynos processor supports the Galaxy Watch Ultra’s enhanced AI abilities, while also ensuring the precision Dual GPS system and next-gen BioActiveSensors can run at full speed. And with an immense battery life, up to 48 hours in Exercise Power Saving mode6, the Galaxy Watch Ultra goes all the way to the finish line, every single time.  
  
The Galaxy Watch Ultra is £599.00 when retailing at full price.

![]()
![]()

## Galaxy Watch7 vs Galaxy Watch Ultra: What are the main differences?

Both the Galaxy Watch Ultra and Watch7 are premium smartwatches that are packed with AI technology and top fitness and wellness features1. The Galaxy Watch7 is available in two sizes; 40mm or 44mm, while the Galaxy Watch Ultra is only available in a 47mm model and is also the heaviest at 94g.   
  
The Galaxy Watch Ultra is specially designed to be super tough and resilient. It boasts a grade 4 titanium casing and has been tested to military standards, so it can keep up with you regardless of altitude, depth or temperature2. In comparison, the Galaxy Watch7 is made to be tough for the everyday and has a strong Armour Aluminium frame that protects it against knocks and scratches.   
  
Both have long-lasting batteries that are optimised to keep you connected throughout the day. However, the Galaxy Watch Ultra has the largest at 590mAh (typical), compared to 300mAh (typical) for the 40mm Galaxy Watch73. Both watches benefit from WPC faster wireless charging – perfect if you need a quick top up before you head out on your next adventure.   
  
You'll still find the wellness features you know and love across the Galaxy Watch7 and Watch Ultra including; Body Composition4, ECG, Blood Pressure5 and women’s health tracking6. ## Galaxy Watch7 vs Galaxy Watch Ultra: Which is the best smartwatch for runners?

The latest Samsung smartwatches offer exceptional health and fitness tracking features for runners. If you love going off the beaten track, the Galaxy Watch Ultra may be your best choice due to its high precision GPS system, military-grade design and emergency safety siren. If you love road running, the less rugged Galaxy Watch7 may be a better choice. It is still tough, but smaller and lighter compared to the Galaxy Watch Ultra. Both support offline music playlists, so you can enjoy your favourite tunes on the new Galaxy Buds3. Plus, with long-lasting battery life, you can enjoy extended runs even with GPS and music playback active.

![]()
![]()

### Galaxy Watch7 vs Galaxy Watch Ultra: Which is the best smartwatch for swimmers?

The Samsung Galaxy Watch7 and Watch Ultra can be worn when swimming thanks to their advanced ‘ATM’ rating which indicates how much pressure the watch can withstand before water begins to penetrate it. The Galaxy Watch7 has a 5ATM1 rating which means it can withstand pressures equivalent to a depth of 50 meters, whereas the 10ATM1 Galaxy Watch Ultra rating doubles that resistance to a whopping 100 meters.

## Galaxy Watch7 vs Galaxy Watch Ultra: Which is the best smartwatch for sleep tracking?

The Galaxy Watch Ultra and Watch7 are equipped with advanced sleep tracking1 features that monitor sleep stages, including REM, light, and deep sleep, throughout the night. By using a combination of motion sensors and heart rate monitoring it can provide detailed insights into your sleep patterns and rest quality. Newly added Sleep Insights offer you a more detailed and accurate analysis of your sleep quality so you can better understand your sleep patterns and build better habits. Galaxy AI evaluates the data to deliver a daily Energy Score which takes into account how much you exercised the day before and how well you slept to help you decide on your wellness goals for the day ahead.   
  
When it comes to the best? The smaller and lightweight design of the Galaxy Watch7 makes it a more comfortable option for sleeping. Its unobtrusive nature allows for a more natural sleep experience, as it’s less likely to disturb you during the night.   
  
Don’t like sleeping with a watch on? Check out the innovative Galaxy Ring which offers a discreet, comfortable alternative for sleep tracking without compromising on functionality. Its sleek design feels like wearing a regular ring, allowing you to monitor your sleep patterns seamlessly.

### Galaxy Watch7 vs Galaxy Watch Ultra: Which is the best smartwatch for fitness & health monitoring?

Both the Galaxy Watch7 and Watch Ultra are equipped with a wide range of innovative fitness features that help you achieve the most from your workouts. As well as tracking exercises, blood pressure2 and heart rate, they can also measure your stress levels and sleep quality. Empowering you to take control of your own health, so you can be your best self.   
  
They both benefit from Samsung's next-gen BioActiveSensor which offers advanced health monitoring. This sensor can measure your body composition1, including your body fat percentage, skeletal muscle mass, and basal metabolic rate2. By having this data at your fingertips, you can better understand your body composition and make informed decisions about your fitness goals, stress levels, and overall health.  
  
Samsung’s newest smartwatches also give detailed insights into your nighttime activity, monitoring everything from time spent in different sleep stages to your snoring habits3. After scoring your sleep quality and providing you with an Energy Score4, they set daily routines and goals to help you achieve your health and fitness goals. In fact, these watches are designed to be your own private coach that never clocks off, constantly analysing your health data from the day to best prepare you for the next.

![]()
![]()

## What AI features come with Samsung smartwatches?

The Galaxy Watch7 and Galaxy Watch Ultra have advanced Galaxy AI features that are designed to provide more personalised insights into your health and wellness. Here’s what you can expect from the latest Samsung wearable tech:  
  
✔ Energy Score1: You can now get a better understanding of your daily condition through a combined analysis of personal health metrics including sleep time average, sleep time consistency, bed/wake time consistency, sleep timing, previous day activity, sleeping heart rate and heart rate variability2.  
  
✔ Wellness Tips1: Offers insights, motivational tips and guidance based on the goals you’re looking to achieve.   
  
✔ Race3: Tracks your progress and keeps you motivated when running or cycling. It compares current and past performance on the same route to help maximise your performance.   
  
✔ Smart Replies4: Galaxy AI now replies to messages for you in your style and voice.   
  
✔ Sleep Insights1: Newly added sleep indicators for Sleep Insights offer you a more detailed and accurate analysis of your sleep quality. These added metrics include movement during sleep, sleep latency, heart rate and respiratory rate during sleep in addition to previously supported metrics like snoring hours, blood oxygen level and sleep cycle.
